expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Rests on item 0: HRC spot ran from the ~$1,150/t the July call assumed to $1,230 (Nucor CSP 10-05) with both EAF peers guiding higher realised prices, against a company statement that Q4 EBITDA will 'even further exceed' the $575M Q3 guide - this name has paid +16%/+21% and -16% on the forward guide, and item 4's 2027 contract reset sits on the same price series (sized down for that overlap); item 1's peer cost misses and item 2's unquantified Stelco idling are the real offsets, and the upside-paid skew (-12.5) plus the Wells Fargo upgrade mean part of this is already in the price, which is what holds p_up at 62 rather than higher.

opus55.note: Q3 HRC spot above the July framing (i0) and the 2027 contract reset (i4) on a guide-driven name with a 13.8% short and upside-paid skew, partly offset by the EAF peers' cost misses (i1) and Stelco (i2); public series, partly priced, so a modest lean on a ~12% move.

sonnet55.note: Rests on HRC spot above the July guide framing (item 0) and the 2027 contract reset, with a 13.8% short and upside-paid skew, partly offset by peer cost misses and the Stelco idling.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0 (HRC spot up through Q3/Q4 against the ~$1,150/t the July call assumed, with the company's own 'even further exceed $575M' Q4 framing) and item 4 (the 2027 contract reset the Street has not underwritten), both landing on the guidance line this name pays on, into a 13.8% short with upside-paid skew; the peer cost-side misses (item 1) and Stelco (item 2) are real but proxy-sized negatives, and the 5-day -6% unwind plus the already upside-paid skew keep p_up at 60 rather than higher.

opus5.note: Four small negatives that point the same way and none that is decisive: PNC missing its own NII guide on funding costs two sessions before FITB prints the same line (item 0, cut as a proxy because Truist landed in line), a guide reaffirmed unchanged on 09-14 against a $1.12 whisper over a $1.09 consensus (item 2), the first quarter carrying post-Comerica-conversion attrition that no model holds (item 3, local-TV sourced so sized small), and item 1's measured reaction function - this name sold a beat-and-raise 2.29% in July and the week's big banks sold beats - all sized against a 1.31% median and 2.29% max realised reaction rather than the 5.79% implied off a 35-day chain.

opus55.note: A slight negative from proxies only: PNC's NII miss on funding costs (i0), a week of banks selling beats with FITB's own beat-and-raise sold last time (i1), and Comerica conversion attrition risk (i3), against a reaffirmed guide and a buyback restart; a 1.3%-median name.

sonnet55.note: A weak lean from PNC's NII miss on funding costs and this week's sold bank beats, against an unchanged guide and a balanced skew.

fable51.note: Nothing company-level and unpriced: the guide is unchanged and the whisper sits above consensus (item 2), PNC missed its own NII guide on funding costs while Truist landed in line (item 0, a mixed proxy), the sector sold beats this week and FITB sold its own beat-and-raise in July (item 1), and the Comerica conversion quarter carries unquantified attrition risk (item 3); light positioning and the buyback restart are small offsets, so a lean down on proxies at p_up 40 over a realistic 2% move, well below the 5.79% the 35-day straddle implies.

opus5.note: Item 0 is the best-researched thing in the pack - ORC -16.6% and IVR -16.1% September book value against DX's ~80% hedge ratio versus their ~100% - but it is a peer-and-rates inference, both 8-Ks were public two days before the seal, and the name's own seven prints have a 0.81% median and 1.8% maximum reaction because an Agency mREIT reprices book intra-quarter; item 1's first October book mark on the call (10yr 5.29% -> 5.09%) cuts the other way and roughly offsets it, so the honest answer here is a small negative, not a conviction name.

opus55.note: The Sept-30 BV drop is priced via the ORC/IVR read-through (i0, slight negative on the lower hedge ratio), against an October-to-date BV recovery likely stated on the call (i1); a name whose prints move under 2%, so near zero.

sonnet55.note: Peer-implied September book value is already near the price, offset by a likely October book-value recovery stated on the call; the stock has moved under 2% on every print.

fable51.note: The Sept-30 book decline is framed by ORC/IVR and the stock already sits at ~1.0x the peer-implied BV (item 0, slightly negative on the lower hedge ratio, though DX tracked ORC in the Q1 widening), so what the print adds is the October 'book value as of Friday' on the call after a 20bp rally in the 10-year and a tighter basis (item 1), plus a small CIO open-market buy; a stock that has moved under 2% on seven prints gets abs 2.0 for an extraordinary quarter and a p_up of 54, near the non-result.
